title: 3-Read Friday #37: Exam Stress, Feedback Loops, and ChatGPT-4o
author: Craig Barton
summary: Issue #37 covers exam-season stress management, independent feedback loops, and a skeptical take on ChatGPT-4o. The InnerDrive team summarises research on exam stress with five practical tips Barton recommends sharing directly with students. Craig Latimir explores how to build 'independent feedback loops' into subjects like maths so students avoid practising -- and automating -- the wrong things. Dan Meyer offers a skeptical response to OpenAI's ChatGPT-4o launch, questioning the viral demo of Sal Khan's son being 'taught' trigonometry by AI. Barton flags Meyer's standing skepticism about AI's potential to 'revolutionise education' as a useful counterweight to the hype.
points: Barton calls the InnerDrive exam-stress research summary 'timely,' specifically recommending its five closing tips as shareable directly with students.

He connects Latimir's 'independent feedback loops' concept to the classic mantra that 'practice makes permanent,' warning that without fast feedback students risk automating errors rather than correcting them.
He flags Dan Meyer as a reliable AI sceptic whose response to the ChatGPT-4o launch questions whether the viral 'Sal Khan's son' demo represents genuine educational progress.
quotes: This is a timely post by the InnerDrive team. They have summarised the key research into exam stress, including links to the original studies should you wish to delve deeper.
The 5 tips at the end are certainly worth sharing with students.
Practice does not make perfect, practice makes permanent, is one of the great education mantras.
Here, Craig explains the importance of independent feedback loops so we can students can ensure students are practising the right skills, and not automating errors.
As regular readers may remember, Dan is very much a sceptic when it comes to the potential for AI to revolutionise education.
